questions.q: What is a stochastic policy π(a|s)?
options: The reward function of the environment
A table of all possible states
A probability distribution over actions, given a state
A mapping that always returns the same action for a given state
questions.explain: A stochastic policy gives a probability distribution π(a|s) over actions in a given state, rather than always choosing the same action deterministically.

questions.q: Why is the discount factor γ necessary in the definition of the return G_t?
options: It converts a stochastic policy into a deterministic one
It guarantees the agent always wins the episode
It keeps the infinite sum of future rewards finite and encodes a preference for sooner reward
It increases the size of the state space
questions.explain: With γ < 1 and bounded rewards, the infinite discounted sum converges, and γ also expresses that reward received sooner is generally worth more than the same reward received later.

questions.q: What does the state-value function V^π(s) represent?
options: The immediate reward received in state s
The expected return starting from state s and following policy π thereafter
The number of actions available in state s
The probability of reaching state s
questions.explain: V^π(s) = E_π[G_t | S_t = s] — the expected discounted return if the agent starts in state s and follows policy π from then on.

questions.q: Why is the action-value function Q^π(s,a) often more directly useful for choosing actions than V^π(s)?
options: Q requires no reward signal to compute
Comparing Q^π(s, a1) to Q^π(s, a2) directly tells you which action is better, without further simulation
Q is always larger in value than V
Q does not depend on the policy π
questions.explain: Because Q already factors in which action is taken, comparing Q-values for different actions in the same state immediately reveals the better action — V alone doesn't separate by action.

questions.q: In RLHF, when a language model is framed as a policy, what does the policy's probability distribution correspond to?
options: The reward model's output score
The distribution over possible next tokens or responses the model can generate
The dataset used to pretrain the model
The learning rate used during fine-tuning
questions.explain: A language model's output distribution over next tokens or full responses is exactly the stochastic policy π(a|s) in this framing — the model's 'action' is the token or response it generates.
